recorded: Both cases passed 11 runs against the unchanged original with Node.js 26.12.1, run as node src/index.ts, the file npm start runs, without its --env-file .env flag, since the lesson ships no environment file and the cases set the variables of the template's .env.example themselves, with Neo4j's address on the cases' own port. The first run downloads Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 from the Hugging Face hub without a token and takes about two minutes, and later runs read the cache. No model is called, and the OpenRouter variables are read but never used. The service is Neo4j 5.14.0 community with APOC, from the lesson's compose file with an override passed on standard input, which gives the container a name of its own, publishes the browser and Bolt on ports 48127 and 48128, leaves out the bind mounts so nothing is written in the module's folder and every run of the file starts with an empty database, and adds a cypher-shell healthcheck, so the services start only once Neo4j answers queries. The output is compared exactly, apart from where the deletion's confirmation falls among the lines of the chunks being added: the original does not wait for the deletion, so the line prints once, usually after the first chunk's. After each run, the cases ask Neo4j's HTTP API, as neo4j with the password password, what the program stored: how many Chunk nodes and distinct ids, their property names, sources, vector sizes, and text lengths, and the vector indexes. The second case runs over what the first stored.

services.up:
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f - -p stackfy-exemplo-12-embeddings-neo4j up -d --wait <<'EOF'
services:
  neo4j:
    container_name: stackfy-exemplo-12-embeddings-neo4j-neo4j
    ports: !override ['48127:7474', '48128:7687']
    volumes: !reset []
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'cypher-shell -u neo4j -p password "RETURN 1"']
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 90
EOF

cases.name: with an empty database, loads the 7 pages of the PDF, splits them into 15 chunks, stores each one with its vector under a cosine index, and prints the three chunks closest to each of the six questions

statements.statement: MATCH (chunk:Chunk) WITH chunk ORDER BY size(chunk.text) RETURN count(chunk) AS chunks, count(DISTINCT chunk.id) AS ids, collect(DISTINCT keys(chunk)) AS properties, collect(DISTINCT chunk.source) AS sources, collect(DISTINCT size(chunk.embedding)) AS dimensions, collect(size(chunk.text)) AS lengths
SHOW INDEXES YIELD name, type, labelsOrTypes, properties, options WHERE type = 'VECTOR' RETURN name, labelsOrTypes, properties, options.indexConfig AS config
